findings.claim: Under a subject-independent evaluation protocol, a multi-scale temporal framework with dynamic fusion achieves 65.22% accuracy for a two-class task and 45.43% accuracy for a three-class task in EEG-based emotion recognition.

evidence.source_text: The best results are 65.22% for the two-class task and 45.43% for the three-class task.

findings.approach: Multi-scale temporal framework with dynamic fusion
findings.architecture: Shared attention-based encoder with dynamic fusion module

findings.claim: In cross-subject and cross-session EEG emotion classification, transfer learning methods achieve the best performance in terms of average classification accuracy.

evidence.source_text: The studies with the best results in terms of average classification accuracy were identified, supporting that transfer learning methods seem to perform better than other approaches.

findings.claim: Integrating Neural-Gas Network features, PSO, and fuzzy logic with XGBoost enhances emotion recognition accuracy using physiological EEG signals.

evidence.source_text: Acquired results indicate that our methodologies enhance the accuracy of emotion recognition systems and outperform other feature selection techniques using the majority of classifiers

findings.approach: PSO Fuzzy XGBoost with NGN features
findings.architecture: Neural-Gas Network (NGN) combined with XGBoost, PSO, and fuzzy logic

findings.claim: Simultaneous spatial-temporal attention achieves the best emotion recognition accuracy compared to other spatial and temporal transformer architectures for EEG.

evidence.source_text: The experimental results demonstrate that simultaneous spatial-temporal attention leads to the best emotion recognition accuracy among the design choices

findings.claim: Evaluation of EEG foundation models across datasets in OmniEEG-Bench uses average rank as a standard metric, showing pretraining dataset diversity and model size correlate with better ranks.

evidence.source_text: Both pretraining dataset diversity and model size are significantly associated with better average ranks across datasets
